messages:
alice_support: customer 8765 reported a leaked API key found in a public repo commit (https://github.com/org/repo/commit/abc123). They want immediate rotation and confirmation of what was accessed. Please advise.

jess_support: opened INC-2026-876, contact carla@cust.com. Short repro: key was baked into a container image and pushed to a registry; logs show calls from 3 distinct IPs. I've attached the commit link to the incident.

security_oncall: @alice_support acknowledged. Immediate plan:
1) Revoke compromised key
2) Issue scoped replacement
3) Gather audit logs (token_id, timestamps, IPs, model/route)
4) Check for request bodies in logs & data retention settings
5) Advise customer to rotate downstream secrets and restart services
I'll take items 1–3 now.

mike_infra: revoked key id key_abc123 at 2024-10-27T15:12Z and created replacement key_new_9f with minimal scopes (embeddings only) and conservative rate limits. Also blocked suspect IPs at the edge.

alice_support: thanks. can you confirm whether hosted audit logs include full prompt contents or just metadata? customer is worried about request body leakage.

security_oncall: Hosted customers: audit logs include metadata (token_id, route, model, latency, response_code, client_ip, timestamp) but NOT full request bodies by default. Detailed request logging is an optional setting and would only be enabled if the tenant opted in or is on a private deployment with forwarded logs. I'm checking tenant settings now to confirm.

devx: For customers that require stronger guarantees we recommend customer-managed KMS/HSM for key material. Pattern: envelope encryption where customer's CMK wraps the API key; rotate CMKs per policy. For HSM roots, we can sign rotation events / audit bundles. Docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/kms-integration (internal link).

jess_support: Draft message to send to customer (internal):
```txt
Hi Carla,

We revoked the compromised key and issued a scoped replacement. Please rotate any downstream deployments and restart services that had the key baked in. We do not see request bodies in hosted audit logs by default; we are collecting metadata logs and will share a redacted export.

Next steps:
- Confirm you rotated all deployed copies and restarted services
- Share any other commit references or indicators of compromise
- Let us know if you need extended audit export or a signed audit bundle for compliance

Thanks,
Redwood Support
```

security_oncall: Added: if they require cryptographic proof of rotation we can provide a signed audit bundle (hashes + signature) within 24 hours. Recommend customer enable customer-managed KMS for Private deployment or use our KMS proxy for higher assurance. Also remind them to rotate any downstream third-party secrets.

infra-bot: action required: incident INC-2026-876 updated by security_oncall — status: in_progress

alice_support: I'll send the draft and ask for confirmation once they rotate. Also requesting explicit permission to share redacted logs with the customer. :thumbsup:

mike_infra: snapshot of relevant audit logs filtered by token_id saved to /mnt/incidents/8765/logs_1719512345.tar.gz (accessible to Security & SRE). I also exported IP and timestamp CSV for quick review.

security_oncall: Quick findings: no evidence of request body exfiltration in hosted logs; only metadata present. No anomalous downstream billing spikes observed. We recommend customer rotate secrets and confirm redeploy. Offering export: hosted logs default retention 90 days; extended retention is available as an enterprise add-on.

alice_support: customer confirmed rotation at 2024-10-27T16:05Z and accepted redacted metadata export. Closing incident pending one final confirmation for compliance export. Thanks everyone :heart:
